name: ghidra
description: Ghidra is a software reverse engineering (SRE) framework
one_liner: A free toolkit, built by the NSA, that lets someone open a compiled program and see roughly how its code works, without having the original source.
buyer: A security consultancy or malware-analysis team that needs to analyze unfamiliar software and currently relies on expensive commercial reverse-engineering tools or scarce specialist staff.
business_use_cases: A security consultancy uses it as the core engine for a malware-analysis and incident-response service, avoiding costly commercial RE tool licenses.
A training company builds and sells a 'learn reverse engineering with Ghidra' certification course for aspiring security analysts.
A software vendor uses it internally to audit their own compiled binaries for accidentally leaked secrets or unintended behavior before release.

money_ideas.idea: Offer paid malware-triage or binary-audit services built on this free tooling, since the software itself cannot be sold.
Sell training, certification, or a curated plugin/script marketplace for analysts who use it daily.

steal_this: Build and sell a focused Ghidra scripting course or plugin pack for one specific niche (say, IoT firmware analysis) where demand already exists but good material is scarce.
